headline: 23 House members (Wilson + 7R/16D) urge Trump to get Musk to let Ukraine use Starlink to hit Russian missile launchers
dek: 23 House members (7 Republicans incl. Wilson, Fitzpatrick, Bacon, Miller, Gimenez, Hurd, Harris; 16 Democrats) wrote Trump urging him to ask Elon Musk to let Ukraine use Starlink to detect/strike Russian missile launchers inside Russia: 'With one phone call, you could save lives while also…
sources: Rep. Joe Wilson letter (via The Hill / mezha); US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (via ABP Live / Asianet Newsable)
fault_line: Should one private billionaire hold the switch on a country's battlefield internet — 'shoot the archer' vs. risk of deep strikes inside Russia?

sections.what_happened: 23 House members (7 Republicans incl. Wilson, Fitzpatrick, Bacon, Miller, Gimenez, Hurd, Harris; 16 Democrats) wrote Trump urging him to ask Elon Musk to let Ukraine use Starlink to detect/strike Russian missile launchers inside Russia: 'With one phone call, you could save lives while also increasing Vladimir Putin's incentives to negotiate... If Ukraine cannot effectively intercept Russian arrows, it should be able to strike the archer.' Separately, Rubio denied Washington ordered any slowdown: 'categorically false. No one at the White House ordered the slowdown'; Starlink is commercial (SpaceX), Starshield is military-only under US contract and 'not available to Ukraine'; Ukraine wants Starshield for deep strikes inside Russia; reported disruption 'has been restored' in his understanding. Context: Oct-15 reports of Starshield/Starlink disruptions complicated Ukrainian air defense; House Foreign Affairs Democrats called it 'unconscionable'; US senators pressing SpaceX for answers.
sections.what_verified: mezha (citing The Hill), ua.news, en.h.ua, english.nv.ua on the letter; ABP Live, Asianet Newsable on Rubio denial; Tribune India / Awaz the Voice on Musk backlash and House Dems criticism; tradersunion on senators pressing SpaceX.
sections.what_disputed: Rubio: no White House involvement, disruption resolved, Starshield is a US-military product Ukraine never had. Musk: Starshield controlled by US government; Starlink commercial, cannot be used for offensive action. Whether Trump was involved in any restriction remains unknown (WSJ via Ukrinform).
sections.why_matters: Congress wants a billionaire's phone call to unlock strikes inside Russia while the same administration is accused of throttling Ukraine's air defense — Washington fights over the switch while Kyiv bleeds.
sections.context: Background: NEW — 23 House members (Wilson + 7R/16D) urge Trump to get Musk to let Ukraine use Starlink to hit Russian missile launchers; Rubio denies any White House-ordered slowdown

totw_analysis: Our read: Congress wants a billionaire's phone call to unlock strikes inside Russia while the same administration is accused of throttling Ukraine's air defense — Washington fights over the switch while Kyiv bleeds. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should one private billionaire hold the switch on a country's battlefield internet — 'shoot the archer' vs. risk of deep strikes inside Russia?
